raw.title: Recruiter
raw.description:
Own Kairos’s hiring and build a recruiting process that can keep up with our rapid growth.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

 

About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

Who we hire over the next year, and how quickly we hire them, will shape which programs Kairos can run and how ambitious they can be. Until now, our hiring has been run by our co-directors and a few staff alongside their other work, so we’re looking for a recruiter to take it on full time. You’d run our hiring rounds, find strong candidates, and build the processes that let us hire well as we grow.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Run Kairos’s hiring rounds end to end. You’ll manage every stage of the pipeline, including application review, work tests, interviews, reference checks, work trials, and offers.

  • Source candidates. Many of our best hires have come to us through people we know, so you’ll draw on our programs, our network, and the broader ecosystem to find strong candidates.

  • Build and improve our hiring infrastructure. You’ll design and refine applications, work tests, interview questions, and candidate tracking. You’ll also think a lot about how AI is changing the way people apply and how we can use it to run hiring better.

  • Help build the team. Beyond running hiring processes, you’ll help scope new roles and weigh in on org design questions, like who we need next and how roles should fit together.

  • Support hiring for Kairos Labs. Kairos Labs, our upcoming incubator for new AI safety organizations, plans to launch in early 2027, and you may help the organizations it supports find their first hires.

 

Who You Are

  • Experience with recruiting. Ideally you’ve run hiring processes before, whether as a recruiter or in a role where hiring was a big part of your work.

  • Strong judgment about people. You’ll make many calls about who should move forward, and you should be comfortable making them well under uncertainty.

  • Good with people. Candidates should enjoy talking with you and come away excited about Kairos.

  • Organized and reliable. We often have 5–10 hiring rounds running at once, so you’ll need to keep track of candidates, interviews, work tests, and work trials across all of them without dropping balls.

  • Mission-aligned with context on AI safety. You care deeply about making advanced AI go well, and you have enough context on the ecosystem to recognize promising people and understand what our roles need.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The people you help us hire over the next year will determine how ambitious Kairos can be, including our capacity to launch new, impactful projects and grow the programs we already run.

  • You’d be Kairos’s first dedicated recruiter, with a lot of room to shape how we hire.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

raw.title: Head of Groups
raw.description:
Own Kairos’s support for AI safety university groups and make it far more ambitious.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

University groups are where many people first get involved in AI safety, and Kairos provides most of the support these groups get today. Through the Pathfinder Fellowship, we provide mentorship and funding to organizers of AI safety university groups around the world, and through OASIS we bring top organizers together for in-person workshops. Over the past year, this work has grown from a fraction of our time to one of our core priorities, and we’re now building a team around it.

We’re looking for a Head of Groups to own this area as a whole and make it more ambitious. You’d set the strategy for how we plan to support AI safety university groups, decide which new initiatives we pursue, and build the team behind them. You would report to Neav Topaz (co-director).

It’d be up to you what the groups team pursues, but we’re weighing several ambitious directions, like hiring full-time organizers in key regions, running residencies for top organizers, seeding new groups at strong universities we’re not yet reaching, and giving the strongest groups much more hands-on support.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Set the strategy for how we support university groups. You’ll decide where the work goes next, how our programs fit together, and what we should start, stop, or scale.

  • Launch new initiatives. You’ll choose which new directions we pursue, like regional organizers, residencies, and focused support for top universities, and get them up and running.

  • Own how we support and fund groups. You’ll set the bar for which groups and organizers we invest in, and decide where our funding goes.

  • Represent the work externally. You’ll be the face of Kairos’s university groups work with organizers, universities, funders, and partner organizations across the ecosystem.

  • Build and lead the groups team. A more ambitious version of this work means bringing on more people. You’ll define the new roles, own their hiring and onboarding, and manage the team as it grows.

  • Contribute to Kairos more broadly. As bandwidth allows, you’ll help shape org-wide strategy, weigh in on new programs, and participate in cross-cutting work.

 

Who You Are

  • Experienced with university groups firsthand. You’ve organized an AI safety university group (or similar), run programs that support them, or worked closely with the organizer ecosystem. We expect the strongest candidates will already know this world well.

  • AI safety context. You have views on how fieldbuilding translates into impact, and enough context on the ecosystem to judge which groups, organizers, and bets are promising.

  • Strong judgment about people. Much of the job is deciding which organizers to back and who to hire, often with limited evidence.

  • Ambitious and high agency. You’re excited to push this work well past its current size and quality bar. You’ll own the portfolio from day one, and should be comfortable building a vision, executing on it autonomously, and answering big open questions as they come up.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about the risks from advanced AI, and you think university groups are one of the most promising ways to help reduce them.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The groups you support are where many future AI safety and policy professionals get their start.

  • University groups are a central part of Kairos’s strategy over the coming years, and you’d own how we scale that work.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $140,000–$195,000 (baseline), $175,000–$245,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $195,000–$270,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, with flexibility for the right candidate

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

 

Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes two months with us, we’ll pay you a $10,000 referral bonus. Learn more here.

raw.title: Generalist (Special Projects)
raw.description:
Join Kairos’s new Special Projects team to help launch and run the tactical projects we take on.

Depending on experience, we consider candidates for the Generalist (Special Projects) or Senior Generalist (Special Projects) version of this role.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

Kairos has historically made a small number of large, ongoing bets, like SPAR and Pathfinder. We’ve learned that a surprising number of time-bound opportunities are worth pursuing too, whether that’s an event, a one-off program, or a project that responds to a narrow window for impact. Our new Special Projects team exists to go after them, and we’re looking for a generalist to help get its projects off the ground.

Some of these projects will be short-lived by design. Others may become lasting programs. Generator went from an idea to a 27-resident cohort at Constellation in a matter of months, and Talent Commons, our shared talent database, will likely become a core part of how Kairos, and much of the AI safety ecosystem, routes talent.

You’d work closely with our Head of Special Projects, doing what each project’s stage needs most, whether that’s recruiting the first participants, running a pilot’s operations, building the systems behind it, or helping figure out whether the idea works at all.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Help launch new projects. You’ll work on one or two early-stage projects at a time, taking on whatever they need to get off the ground.

  • Build the systems behind them. You’ll set up the infrastructure new projects run on, like applications, communications, and automations, so a pilot can grow into a program.

  • Grow with the work. You’ll take on more ownership as projects mature, and the shape of the role will evolve with your strengths and interests.

  • Pitch in on broader Kairos work as capacity allows. You’ll help on active programs like SPAR, Pathfinder, and Generator, build relationships across the AI safety ecosystem, and ship small cross-team projects.

 

Who You Are

  • You want to do many things well, pick up new domains quickly, and work on whatever is most useful rather than settle into a fixed lane.

  • High agency. Early-stage projects come with little structure. You figure out what needs doing and do it, without waiting to be asked.

  • Fast and scrappy. You ship quickly, iterate as you learn, and are okay with unglamorous operational work along the way.

  • Mission-aligned with context on AI safety. You care deeply about making advanced AI go well, and you’re familiar enough with the ecosystem to understand the gaps our new projects aim to fill.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The projects you help build could become Kairos’s next core programs and address critical bottlenecks in AI safety.

  • Few roles offer this much variety. You’ll touch several programs and projects in your first year, and we’ll shape the role around your comparative advantage.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

  • Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying

  • Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US

  • We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston.

  • We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1).

  • Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

raw.title: GCP Program Manager
raw.description:
Build and lead residential workshops that help exceptional people pursue high-impact work in AI safety, biosecurity, and policy.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

The Global Challenges Project (GCP) runs three-day residential workshops that help talented individuals explore careers in AI safety and biosecurity. Over the past few years, GCP has run dozens of workshops for 400+ students, mostly in Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. GCP has a long and successful track record and became part of Kairos in early 2026.

We’re now expanding GCP into a full portfolio of workshops serving different audiences and career stages, with the ambition of becoming the leading fieldbuilding workshop organizer in AI safety and biosecurity. This means building new programs, new formats, and the systems to deliver reliably at scale.

We’re looking for a GCP Program Manager to build and lead at least two strands of our expanding workshop portfolio, reporting to Sam Glendenning, who leads the Global Challenges Project.

You’ll have broad ownership of your programs, from deciding what they should achieve and who they should serve through to delivering the workshops themselves. This includes outreach and marketing strategy, participant selection, guest recruitment, workshop design, team leadership, in-person delivery, and impact evaluation.

This is an unusually hands-on role. You’ll shape the strategy behind your programs, build the systems needed to run them effectively, and then lead them in person. Because we run our portfolio experimentally, individual programs may change or be discontinued, but this role is not tied to any single program. You’ll own a portfolio that evolves as we learn what works.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own two or more GCP programs. You’ll take responsibility for their strategy, design, delivery, and evaluation. Programs you may own include:

    • Workshops for students newer to AI safety, for professionals considering a pivot into AI safety, or for accelerating people into politics or policy

    • Workshop support for other organizations, from advice and coordination to running workshops on their behalf

    • A high-impact format you propose (we’re open to strong cases for new programs)

  • Run programs experimentally. We’re testing which of these programs offer the most value to the ecosystem. You’ll experiment with both the format and purpose of your workshops, and be willing to discontinue programs that aren’t working, even after investing significant time in them.

  • Own outreach and participant selection. You’ll develop marketing and outreach strategies, build strong applicant pools, and decide who will benefit most from attending each program.

  • Build relationships and recruit guests. High-quality guests are central to the impact of our workshops. You’ll proactively build relationships across the field and invite researchers, policymakers, funders, operators, and other experts to participate.

  • Design excellent workshops. You’ll develop the structure, sessions, content, and participant experience for each program, holding everything to a very high standard.

  • Lead workshops in person. You’ll give talks, introduce guests, advise participants, manage the team on the ground, and take responsibility for how well each workshop runs.

  • Lead your program teams. We organize delivery program by program. You’ll direct the work of the GCP team, interns, and volunteers on your programs (typically three to four people per workshop). Once the team grows, you’ll likely line-manage one GCP team member and our interns.

  • Measure impact and iterate. You’ll collect structured feedback at every workshop, track participant outcomes over the following months, and use the evidence to improve, scale, or discontinue programs.

  • Help GCP scale. You’ll contribute to team-wide strategy, build operational structures and automation that let us expand without compromising quality, and help design and launch our internship program.

 

Who You Are

  • Experienced at running events. You’ve organized and delivered events such as workshops, conferences, or retreats, and you’re comfortable making game-time decisions. Strong project delivery experience in complex in-person settings can substitute.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about how the development of advanced AI and biotechnology plays out, and you believe workshops can be a highly effective way to help talented people enter these fields.

  • Good with people, and energized by workshops. Leading three-day residential events is central to this role. You’ll need the energy to engage with participants and guests throughout while keeping the event running smoothly.

  • Comfortable managing a small team. Within a year, you’ll likely begin managing 2 or more people. Prior experience managing operational or programmatic teams is a strong plus.

  • High agency. You’ll have significant ownership over your programs, and we expect you to spot problems early, adapt when plans change, and fix things without waiting to be asked.

  • Highly organized. You’ll oversee several programs simultaneously, each with different workstreams, teams, and deadlines. You’ll need strong systems for keeping everything on track.

  • Familiar with the AI safety ecosystem. You know the major organizations and people in the field and understand how its parts fit together. You use that context to make good strategic decisions and to point participants toward the right opportunities. Familiarity with biosecurity or US policy is a plus, and matters more for some programs than others.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll work toward reducing risks from advanced AI and biotechnology, two of the most important challenges of our time. Both fields need far more talented people than they have, and our workshops move promising people into careers working on them.

  • You’ll build and develop your own programs, lead the teams delivering them, and see the results firsthand.

  • GCP already has a strong brand, an excellent reputation, and a long track record. You’ll build on one of the ecosystem’s most successful workshop programs while joining a team with the ambition to become the leading workshop organizer in the space.

  • You’ll work closely with high-profile guests across AI safety and biorisk, developing a strong professional network.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $140,000–$195,000 (baseline), $175,000–$245,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $195,000–$270,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, with flexibility for the right candidate

  • This is a remote role, with travel roughly 8 to 12 times a year (typically 3 to 6 days at a time) for workshops, conferences, and events, predominantly in the UK and US.

  • We’re a remote-first organization, but because of how the GCP team works, we have a preference for candidates within five hours of UK time. Our current team spans GMT-8 to GMT+1, and we’ll gladly consider exceptional candidates elsewhere, including in the US.

  • We may be able to sponsor visas for the UK or US, depending on individual circumstances, including but not limited to O-1A visas. We can’t make guarantees regarding visa approval.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

 

Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes two months with us, we’ll pay you a $10,000 referral bonus. Learn more here.

  • London, DC, Boston, NYC • $175K – $245K
  • San Francisco Bay Area • $195K – $270K

raw.title: Generalist (Workshops)
raw.description:
Deliver workshops that help exceptional people pursue high-impact work in AI safety, biosecurity, and policy.

Depending on experience, we consider candidates for the Generalist (Workshops) or Senior Generalist (Workshops) version of this role.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

The Global Challenges Project (GCP) runs three-day residential workshops that help talented individuals explore careers in AI safety and biosecurity. Over the past few years, GCP has run dozens of workshops for 400+ students, mostly in Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. GCP has a long and successful track record and became part of Kairos in early 2026.

We’re now expanding GCP into a full portfolio of workshops serving different audiences and career stages, with the ambition of becoming the leading fieldbuilding workshop organizer in AI safety and biosecurity. This means building new programs, new formats, and the systems to deliver reliably at scale.

We’re looking for a generalist to help deliver our workshops. You’ll own the operational backbone of our events, including outreach, venues, travel, admissions logistics, guest coordination, inventory, and the systems that hold it all together. You’ll also attend some of our workshops and help run them in person.

This job requires agency as you’ll own the delivery of many key aspects of our workshops. You’ll need to spot problems before they happen, and improve our strategy and systems after every event. This role offers excellent opportunities for progression, and your scope and responsibility will grow with our portfolio.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own operational workstreams end to end. For each workshop, you’ll take responsibility for workstreams such as outreach, venue search and contracting, catering and dietary needs, participant and guest travel, inventory and materials, and on-site logistics.

  • Run admissions and participant operations. You’ll build application and RSVP forms, help coordinate selection processes, send decisions, run onboarding communications, and make sure every participant arrives informed and prepared.

  • Coordinate guests. High-quality guests are central to our workshops’ impact. You’ll track invitations, chase confirmations, and act as a point of contact so guests have a smooth experience from first email to follow-up.

  • Deliver workshops in person. You’ll travel to some of our workshops (predominantly in the UK and US) and help run them on the ground.

  • Build systems that scale. We run our events on Notion, Airtable, Linear, and a growing set of automations and custom code. You’ll help design and improve these systems and turn what we learn at each event into better playbooks and templates.

  • Help shape our workshops strategy. You’ll work across GCP, OASIS, and our new workshop programs, and everyone on the team has a say in how Kairos’s events develop.

  • Contribute to Kairos more broadly. As capacity allows, you’ll pitch in on our other programs like SPAR and Pathfinder, build relationships across the AI safety ecosystem, and ship small cross-team projects.

 

Who You Are

  • An operations generalist with events experience. You’ve delivered events such as workshops, conferences, or retreats, or you’ve done demanding operational work and can show you’d thrive doing it for in-person events.

  • Highly organized. You’ll juggle multiple workstreams across several workshops at once, each with its own deadlines. You have strong systems for keeping everything on track, and details don’t slip past you.

  • High agency. You spot problems early and fix them without waiting to be asked, and you adapt when plans change on the day.

  • A high quality bar. You check your own work before handing it over, and you care about getting the small things right because they’re important to the attendees’ experience.

  • Good with people, and energized by workshops. Attending three-day residential events is part of this role. You’ll need the energy to engage warmly with participants and guests while keeping the event running smoothly.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about how the development of advanced AI and biotechnology plays out, and you believe workshops can be a highly effective way to help talented people enter these fields. Familiarity with the AI safety ecosystem is a plus, but not required.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll work toward reducing risks from advanced AI and biotechnology, two of the most important challenges of our time. Both fields need far more talented people than they have, and our workshops move promising people into careers working on them. The quality of our delivery is a big part of that impact.

  • You’ll own your workstreams end to end, and you’ll see the results firsthand at every workshop.

  • You’ll build on GCP’s strong brand, excellent reputation, and long track record, and help us grow into the leading workshop organizer in the space.

  • You’ll work closely with high-profile guests across AI safety and biorisk, and develop a strong professional network.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, with flexibility for the right candidate

  • This is a remote role, with travel roughly 8 to 12 times a year (typically 3 to 6 days at a time) for workshops, conferences, and events, predominantly in the UK and US.

  • We’re a remote-first organization, but because much of our workshop work happens on UK time, we have a preference for candidates within five hours of UK time. Our current team spans GMT-8 to GMT+1, and we’ll gladly consider exceptional candidates elsewhere, including in the US.

  • We may be able to sponsor visas for the UK or US, depending on individual circumstances, including but not limited to O-1A visas. We can’t make guarantees regarding visa approval.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more →

 

Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes two months with us, we’ll pay you a $10,000 referral bonus. Learn more here.

  • Most locations (baseline) • $105K – $145K
  • London, DC, Boston, NYC • $130K – $180K
  • San Francisco Bay Area • $145K – $200K

title: Founders Associate (m/w/d)
description: Bei GALVANY ist es unser Ziel, klimaneutrales Wohnen für alle zur Realität zu machen. Wir setzen auf Umsetzung und entwickeln konkrete, smarte Lösungen, indem wir Wärmepumpen, Batteriespeicher und Smart Metering einfach zugänglich, zuverlässig und bezahlbar machen. Wir sind ein profitables Greentech-Startup und glauben, dass nachhaltiger Impact und langfristiges Wachstum nur auf Basis eines gesunden Geschäftsmodells möglich sind. Um unsere ambitionierte Tech Roadmap umzusetzen haben wir im Frühjahr 2026 eine Seed-Finanzierung in Höhe von 10 Millionen Euro mit Set Ventures und AENU abgeschlossen. Getrieben von Kundennutzen, Klarheit und Verantwortung stehen wir für hochwertige Heizlösungen und ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Menschen Verantwortung übernehmen und nachhaltigen Mehrwert schaffen. Als Founders Associate CEO Office (m/w/d) bei GALVANY arbeitest du im CEO-Office direkt mit unserem Gründer Raik und dem Leadership-Team zusammen. Du treibst strategische und operative Themen quer durch das Unternehmen. Du wirst Teil eines Teams, das Erfahrungen aus Top-Strategieberatungen (MBB), Unicorns und Private Equity mitbringt und von führenden Universitäten wie TUM, INSEAD und Berkeley kommt. Deine Aufgaben GTM: Du treibst Growth-Initiativen in einem schnell wachsenden Start-up voran, entwickelst datenbasierte Go-to-Market-Strategien und setzt diese um– von der ersten Marktanalyse bis zum Launch neuer Produkte mit ersten Partnern. Cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest eng mit Sales, Marketing, Product und Customer Success zusammen, um die Customer Journey abteilungsübergreifend zu koordinieren, Reibungsverluste zu minimieren und eine gemeinsame Strategie umzusetzen. Prozessaufbau & -optimierung: Du baust Prozesse von Grund auf, dokumentierst sie sauber und entwickelst sie kontinuierlich weiter. Du denkst in Strukturen, erkennst Ineffizienzen früh und setzt Verbesserungen hands-on um. Research & strategische Analyse: Du führst eigenständig Markt-, Wettbewerbs- und Potenzialanalysen durch, leitest konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen ab und bereitest Ergebnisse für das Leadership-Team auf. Strategische Partnerschaften: Du identifizierst relevante Partner, bereitest Erstgespräche vor, unterstützt bei der Entwicklung von Value Propositions und begleitest den Aufbau strategischer Kooperationen von der Ansprache bis zur Vereinbarung. AI & Automation: Du identifizierst Automatisierungspotenziale in internen Prozessen und Geschäftsmodellen, testest KI-Tools und -Workflows und trägst aktiv dazu bei, wie Galvany künstliche Intelligenz operativ einsetzt – zur Effizienzsteigerung, Produktentwicklung und Entscheidungsfindung. Dein Profil Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Master Studium an einer Top-Universität in einem wirtschaftswissenschaftlichen Studiengang. Du hast erste praktische Erfahrungen in einem dynamischen Umfeld gesammelt z. B. in einem Start-up, einer Unternehmensberatung oder einem VC. Du denkst strukturiert, analytisch und zahlenaffin und kannst komplexe Sachverhalte schnell durchdringen, sauber aufbereiten und klar kommunizieren. Du trittst sicher auf und überzeugst unterschiedliche Stakeholder, intern wie extern, durch präzise, verständliche Kommunikation, auch in anspruchsvollen Situationen. Du arbeitest selbstständig, bringst Themen eigenverantwortlich voran und verlierst auch in einem schnellen, sich verändernden Umfeld nicht den Überblick. Du bist neugierig auf KI-Tools und Automatisierung und hast idealerweise bereits erste Erfahrungen damit gesammelt oder den Willen, dich schnell einzuarbeiten. Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift. Zusätzlich sind uns folgende Fähigkeiten und Eigenschaften wichtig: Entrepreneurial Mindset: Du übernimmst Verantwortung, handelst proaktiv und machst aus Unklarheit eine Chance. Du verbindest Kreativität mit einem Macher-Mindset, um Dinge voranzubringen. Methodical: Du denkst und arbeitest geordnet, klar und nachvollziehbar – in deinen Gedankengängen genauso wie in der Art, wie du Informationen aufbereitest und präsentierst. Strategic Thinker: Du planst über den nächsten Monat hinaus, erkennst frühzeitig, was das Team in 6–12 Monaten braucht, und bringst die richtigen Initiativen auf den Weg. Clear Communicator: Du kannst komplexe Themen für unterschiedliche Zielgruppen verständlich aufbereiten – schriftlich wie mündlich – und bleibst auch in schwierigen Situationen sachlich und klar. Collaborative: Du arbeitest eng mit verschiedenen Teams zusammen – von Sales über Marketing bis hin zu Operations – um Botschaften und Strategie aufeinander abzustimmen. Benefits Werde Teil eines schnell wachsenden und profitablen Climate-Tech-Startups Attraktive und wettbewerbsfähige Vergütung Unser lebendiges Office ist das Herz unserer Kultur und fördert Zusammenarbeit und Austausch vor Ort Individuelle Benefits, abgestimmt auf deine Bedürfnisse, z. title: General Manager (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand
description: Managing Director (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand Location: Köln Start: Ab sofort Setup: Vollzeit (on-site) THE BRAND & THE OPPORTUNITY Du baust gemeinsam mit uns eine neue Fitness-Marke im Segment Mid Cost - High Value auf. Die Vision: „ Der neue Hotspot in der City für Workout, Recovery, Co-Working und Socializing.“ Kraft, Cardio und Functional, Live-Kurse, Sauna und Recovery, Bar und Lounge sowie eine ruhige Co-Working Zone, alles unter einem Dach - zu einem erschwinglichen Preis deutlich unter Premium-Clubs. Unsere Clubs sollen auf ehemaligen Retail-Flächen entstehen, in 1A-Innenstadtlagen mit langfristig gesicherten Mietverträgen. Wir starten in Westdeutschland in der Region Köln, Essen, Frankfurt und expandieren dann. Wir arbeiten mit unternehmerischem Anspruch: kleines Team, kurze Wege, jeder Standort muss sich selbst tragen. Der erste Club ist der Beweis für das Konzept, und jeder weitere wird durch den Erfolg des vorherigen verdient. Für dich heißt das: Du bist ab Sekunde 1 dabei und gestaltest vom Namen über das Konzept bis hin zur Location alles von Grund auf mit. Kein Einstieg in einen bestehenden Betrieb, sondern die Chance, eine Marke von Null an aufzubauen , das Modell in allen Details zu gestalten und volle Verantwortung für das Ergebnis zu übernehmen. THE ROLE & YOUR ROADMAP Als Managing Director verantwortest du den kompletten Aufbau der Marke - von den ersten Entwürfen auf dem Reißbrett bis hin zur Multi-Site-Skalierung. Phase 1 - Konzept schärfen: Du bringst das Angebot, das Flächenprogramm, die Pricing-Strategie und den Brand-Auftritt gemeinsam mit den Gesellschaftern zur Marktreife. Phase 2 - Ersten Club eröffnen: Du steuerst den Ausbau vor Ort, baust dein Kernteam auf, drehst den Pre-Opening-Sales auf Anschlag und bringst den ersten Flagship-Standort ans Netz. Phase 3 - Proof of Concept: Du erreichst mit dem Club die geplanten Mitglieder- und Ergebniszahlen (P&L) und machst aus dem Piloten ein hocheffizientes, wiederholbares Modell. Phase 4 - Skalieren: Du eröffnest weitere Standorte in Deutschland und baust die Organisation auf, die dieses Wachstum trägt. At Ambrosys, we build data-driven systems for complex mobility and urban infrastructure challenges (B2B/B2G), including traffic insights, geolocation, tolling, and smart city solutions.

In this role, you will solve Ambrosys’s core sales bottleneck—taking end-to-end ownership of pipeline growth, new account acquisition across the DACH region, and strategic key account expansion. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will partner with key stakeholders—including the CTO, GTM, and Product teams—to translate client goals into high-value technical solutions and drive top-line growth.

Sales Strategy Development: Develop and implement a comprehensive sales strategy that aligns with Ambrosys’s objectives and product portfolio to drive revenue growth. You will own end-to-end B2B and B2G sales cycles, from initial outreach and consultative deal closing through account expansion.
Market Expansion: Identify new business opportunities to expand Ambrosys’s footprint within industry verticals. You will manage new market entries and qualify high-value opportunities by testing ICP hypotheses, uncovering core pain points, and mapping buying centers and budgets.
Customer Relationship Management: Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with key accounts, partners, and stakeholders, ensuring a deep understanding of customer needs.
Collaboration: Work closely with the CEO, the CTO, GTM-team and Product leads to ensure alignment on sales goals, custom offers, pricing strategies, and contract negotiations.
Revenue Management: Align with ambitious sales targets, monitor performance metrics with high ownership, and meet revenue goals while maintaining profitability.
Forecasting & Reporting: Provide accurate and timely sales forecasts, reports, and insights to the CEO and CTO to enable data-driven decision-making.
Innovation: Stay ahead of industry trends and emerging technologies to continually refine sales approaches. Master complex technical domains like Agentic AI and real-time mobility platforms to articulate product value credibly.


Your profile


  • Experience: 8+ years of experience in enterprise or IT solution sales, with a significant portion within the technology sector of mobility, tolling, traffic, or logistics

  • Demonstrated success in driving revenue growth, managing sales pipelines and expanding market share in the region.

  • Proven ability to manage through change and ambiguity in a dynamic market.

  • Exceptional strategic and analytical thinking skills, with a history of developing and executing successful sales strategies.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise customer needs and the ability to build lasting, trusted relationships with key decision-makers.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence at all levels of the organization.

  • Degree in business administration, industrial engineering, business informatics, or comparable experience

  • Professional fluency in both German & English is a must


Why us?

As a new member of our team, you can look forward to:

  • Exciting and diverse tasks and close collaboration in small teams
  • A flexible work schedule and location, with up to 4 days a week from home
  • The ability to work from abroad for a total of 10 days per year
  • A personal training and career development plan, including a generous €1,500 yearly learning budget for further education
  • Regular company and team events, including our monthly meetup to connect, exchange ideas, and have fun together
  • A flat hierarchy and open communication channels with direct access to the CEO
  • A dedicated feel-good manager providing best-in-town coffee, refreshments, fresh fruit/vegetables, snacks, and a monthly company breakfast
  • Optional bike leasing with a discount for a stress-free commute
  • A subsidised Deutschlandticket for easy commuting
  • Additional days off for special occasions or if your child is ill

As an equal opportunities employer, we welcome and value diversity and inclusivity. We encourage applications from all qualified individuals, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, religion, belief, or age.

Important note: We manage our recruitment process entirely in-house and do not collaborate with external recruiters. Please refrain from sending unsolicited profiles or outreach.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Platform & Infrastructure (f/m/d)
description: The product you will work on The HOLOPLOT Matrix Array is a new type of sound system built around precise, software-defined control of sound in three dimensions - grounded in physics and implemented through a combination of custom hardware and purpose-built software. HOLOPLOT deployed Matrix Arrays in various venues, including the Sphere in Las Vegas - the world’s most advanced entertainment venue and, notably, home to the world’s largest audio installation in entertainment. Audio processing in HOLOPLOT systems is distributed: every loudspeaker runs embedded Linux, and hundreds of them have to be configured, coordinated, monitored, and updated as one system. This is enabled by multiple open source and in-house developed services running on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster. AWS-hosted services connect venues to remote monitoring, telemetry, and configuration. Many venues are air-gapped or only intermittently connected for remote servicing, and that constraint shapes most of the design decisions in the platform. The ideal candidate is We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who builds the platform our sound systems run on, and who takes responsibility for how it behaves in production. This is a software engineering role first. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field. Your role and responsibilities You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams. Build the platform Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters. Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions. Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment. Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations. Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services. Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior . Run what you build Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code. Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations. Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code. Be part of a compensated on-call rotation Set the technical direction Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind. Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate. Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes. What you need to succeed in this role Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems. Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on. Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy. Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today. Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack. Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation. A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change. A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation. Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems. Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone. Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists. Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it. A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone. Experience in using AI for engineering. Nice to haves Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production. Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations. Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it. Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security. Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6. Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry. Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects We offer you At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme. You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership. You’ll work on cutting-edge audio technology, turn complex requirements into working solutions and contribute to global projects, with support for your growth through individual development plans, mentoring and coaching. You will spend your time writing software, either with your own team or embedded with one of the other HOLOPLOT teams: services, controllers, agents, and tooling that provision, configure, observe, and update our systems. Our infrastructure is defined as code and evolves through the same review and release process as the rest of our software. You design the operational side, you build it, and you are on call when it misbehaves in the field.


Your role and responsibilities

You will join the team that owns the platform underneath our installations and connected services, working alongside backend, embedded, and frontend engineers who are organized in cross-functional product teams.


Build the platform

  • Architect and implement services to provision, configure, and manage server fleets across AWS and local clusters.

  • Create control-plane logic for venue systems to ensure consistency, health monitoring, rollout management, and recovery, even during uplink disruptions.

  • Establish end-to-end provisioning workflows for embedded Linux hardware, spanning from initial manufacturing to customer deployment.

  • Enhance update processes to streamline software deployments for active customer installations.

  • Develop APIs and developer tooling that empower engineering teams to independently deploy, observe, and troubleshoot their services.

  • Embed telemetry capabilities into the platform to facilitate remote diagnosis of venue system behavior

  • .

Run what you build

  • Own the AWS infrastructure behind our connected services: remote access, access control, telemetry ingestion, remote backup, secret management, and monitoring. All of it is infrastructure as code.

  • Operate and evolve the on-premises Kubernetes footprint at venues, including air-gapped and intermittently connected installations.

  • Monitor large environments, investigate problems across the software/hardware boundary, and turn each incident into a fix in the code.

  • Be part of a compensated on-call rotation


Set the technical direction

  • Advise and collaborate with product teams on building distributed systems that are scalable, secure, and observable, and review their designs with production reality in mind.

  • Research and introduce tools and technologies where they measurably improve how we build and operate.

  • Contribute back to the open-source projects we depend on, through issues and fixes.


What you need to succeed in this role

  • Several years of professional software engineering experience, most of it spent designing and shipping production systems.

  • Fluency in software engineering as a craft: concurrency, error handling, testing, and designing APIs that other teams build on.

  • Working knowledge of the Kubernetes control plane and the operator/controller pattern, including how clusters behave when they are unhealthy.

  • Hands-on experience with AWS, and a firm belief in infrastructure as code. Terraform and Ansible are what we use today.

  • Comfort across several languages, and the ability to pick up a new one when the problem calls for it. Our platform work is mostly Go and Python, with Rust and C++ elsewhere in the stack.

  • Experience building distributed systems, and a clear understanding of how they fail: partitions, partial rollouts, clock skew, retries, and reconciliation.

  • A good sense for software architecture and maintainability, and the habit of writing code that colleagues can pick up and change.

  • A strong command of Linux, scripting, and automation.

  • Experience instrumenting software for telemetry and using it to answer real questions about running systems.

  • Good judgment about what to automate and what to leave alone.

  • Strong communication skills in English. You can explain a design or a failure clearly to engineers, product stakeholders, and non-specialists.

  • Willingness to take part in compensated on-call and weekend work when installations need it.

  • A can-do mentality, an eye for detail, and the courage to take on problems outside your comfort zone.

  • Experience in using AI for engineering.


Nice to haves

  • Experience with NATS, Prometheus/Thanos, or PostgreSQL in production.

  • Experience with air-gapped or intermittently connected installations.

  • Experience running Kubernetes in production, not only deploying to it.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, device fleet management, or IoT security.

  • Networking depth: multicast at scale, WireGuard, BGP, IPv6.

  • Experience in the audio, broadcast, or live events industry.

  • Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects


We offer you

At HOLOPLOT we work in a flexible hybrid setup with trust-based working hours, giving you the freedom to organise your day in a way that supports focus, deep work and balance. Pay is competitive and fair, and we offer perks and benefits such as subsidised public transport, lunch allowances, Urban Sports and a company pension scheme.

You’ll join an international, open-minded team across software, hardware, product and research, in an environment with plenty of autonomy and ownership. You’ll work on cutting-edge audio technology, turn complex requirements into working solutions and contribute to global projects, with support for your growth through individual development plans, mentoring and coaching.

title: Senior Expert*in Energieberatung – Fachentwicklung
description: Deine Verantwortung Tiefes Produkt- und Prozessverständnis als Fundament – Du kennst unsere Produkte, Prozesse und Dienstleistungen im Detail und verstehst, wie die Energieberatung bei uns tatsächlich arbeitet. Dieses Wissen ist die Grundlage für alles, was du in der Rolle bewegst. Produktivität und KPIs konsequent im Blick – Du analysierst, wie die Energieberatung produktiver und effizienter werden kann, und verknüpfst diese Erkenntnisse mit unserer Pricing-Strategie. Prozesse und Strukturen gemeinsam mit Tech & Product entwickeln – Den Großteil deiner Zeit verbringst du in enger Zusammenarbeit mit Tech & Product: Ihr entwickelt Prozesse, Strukturen und teilweise neue Produkte, damit die Energieberatung effizienter arbeitet. Du denkst dabei nicht nur mit, sondern treibst die Optimierung aktiv voran. Überblick über unser Dienstleistungsportfolio – Du behältst den Blick fürs Ganze: Welche neuen Themen und Dienstleistungen nehmen wir zusätzlich in unser Angebot auf, wie attraktiv sind sie für den Markt? Deine Einschätzung entscheidet mit, wie sich unser Angebot am Markt weiterentwickelt. Fachliche Koordination & Weiterentwicklung der Energieberatung – Du bewertest, ob ein neues Thema intern von bestehenden Mitarbeitenden übernommen werden kann oder ob wir extern ein passendes Profil aufbauen müssen. Darüber hinaus koordinierst du die fachliche Weiterentwicklung der Energieberatung, behältst Lizenzen und Richtlinien im Blick und steuerst Trainings – ohne sie selbst operativ durchzuführen. Dein Profil Fachlich fundiert – Du hast ein Studium als Ingenieur*in oder Architekt*in abgeschlossen, bringst fundierte Erfahrung aus der Energieberatung mit und kennst die Arbeitsweise im Consulting-Kontext aus eigener Praxis. Analytisches Denken & wirtschaftliches Gespür – Du hast ein sicheres Marktverständnis und bewertest fundiert, ob sich ein Produkt oder eine Dienstleistung wirtschaftlich trägt – mit Blick auf Preis und Aufwand, sowohl bei bestehenden als auch bei potenziellen neuen Angeboten. Pragmatismus, Tempo & Ergebnisorientierung – Du setzt Prioritäten dort, wo sie den größten Unterschied machen, und sorgst dafür, dass aus Überlegungen konkrete Ergebnisse werden. Kommunikationsstark & flexibel im Zusammenspiel – Du bringst deine fachliche Einschätzung klar und überzeugend ein – im Austausch mit Kolleg*innen ebenso wie mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern – und arbeitest dabei eng mit einem weiteren Tribe Lead zusammen. Sprachlich sattelfest – Deutsch auf C2-Niveau, Englisch mindestens B2. Fuchs & Eule Wir nehmen unsere Verantwortung für eine grüne Zukunft ernst und wollen mit unserem Einsatz für Energieeffizienz einen deutlichen Beitrag zur CO2-Reduktion zu leisten. Wir sind ambitioniert und wollen immer besser werden . Deswegen geben wir Dir Spielraum und Verantwortung, wo Du Dich weiterentwickeln möchtest und Unterstützung, wo Du sie brauchst. Wir sind digital, innovativ, kundenzentriert und hochmotiviert mit Dir zusammen Großes zu schaffen. Wir sind ein echtes Team und stehen füreinander ein, sagen was wir denken, haben gemeinsam Spaß und das Herz am rechten Fleck. Uns ist es wichtig, dass wir uns regelmäßig persönlich begegnen, deswegen haben wir unser Büro mit viel Liebe ausgewählt und gestaltet. Wir legen großen Wert auf Team Events und gleichzeitig auch auf Flexibilität. Deswegen sind zwei Tage Home Office pro Woche bei uns der Standard. Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

Mit unseren Produkten haben wir eine eigene Kategorie geformt: Smart Food. In ganz Europa unterwegs, rasant wachsend und immer auf der Suche nach neuen Ideen. Wenn du Teil eines dynamischen Teams sein möchtest, das die Lebensmittelbranche revolutioniert, dann bist du bei yfood genau richtig. Deine Aufgaben als Key Account Manager im Handel Als Key Account Manager im einstufigen Handel fungierst du als Sprachrohr von yfood in den Handel und bist eine wichtige Schnittstelle zu unserem Außendienst. Als Teil eines erfahrenen und dynamischen Key Account Management Teams gestaltest du das Geschäft und den nachhaltigen Erfolg aktiv mit und bist wichtiger Impulsgeber für unser Unternehmen. Strategische Planung, Betreuung und konzeptionelle Weiterentwicklung der zu verantwortenden Kunden im einstufigen Key Account Management (z.B Globus, Bünting, Bartels-Langness, Klaas & Kock) Planung und Erreichung der unternehmerischen Umsatz-, Absatz-, Ertrags- und Distributionsziele Um- und Durchsetzung nationaler Absprachen sowie Durchsetzung der nationalen, konzeptionellen und strategischen Vertriebs- und Marketingziele Analysen von KPI`s, Markt- und Absatzdaten mit entsprechender Ableitung von Maßnahmen Vorbereitung, Teilnahme und Nachbereitung von regelmäßigen Kunden- und Jahresgesprächen Absprache und Umsetzung von Aktionen, Listungen und Preisstrategien, sowie kundenindividuellen Maßnahmen Auf- und Ausbau konstruktiver Beziehungen zu allen relevanten Entscheidern und regelmäßiger Austausch Enge Zusammenarbeit mit allen Key Account Managern zur Koordination bzw. Abstimmung einer zielgerichteten Vorgehensweise Kommunikation und Abstimmung mit den Schnittstellen Logistik, Finance, Marketing, Trade Marketing und der nationalen Field Sales Force DAS MACHT DICH AUS Deine Qualifikationen als Key Account Manager im Handel Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium der Betriebswirtschaftslehre oder vergleichbare kaufmännische Ausbildung Mindestens 3 Jahre Berufserfahrung im Key Account Management, tiefes Wissen über die Abläufe der Handelsstruktur und gute Kontakte zu den Entscheidern der Handelsbranche. Außendiensterfahrung wünschenswert Ausgeprägte analytische und konzeptionelle Fähigkeiten sowie Stärke, mehrere wichtige Themen und Projekte gleichzeitig zu treiben Kommunikationsstarke und teamorientierte Persönlichkeit mit hoher Eigeninitiative, Lösungsorientierung und Konfliktfähigkeit WAS UNS ANTREIBT Wir sind ein bisschen anders – und genau das macht uns aus: Leidenschaft – Wir brennen für das, was wir tun. Voller Energie, voller Optimismus, immer hungrig nach Neuem. Verantwortung – Heißt für uns: Füreinander einstehen, Verantwortung übernehmen und alles geben, wenn’s drauf ankommt. Professionalität – Wir nehmen unsere Arbeit ernst – uns selbst aber nicht zu sehr. Wir sind offen, direkt und immer auf Augenhöhe. Kein Bullshit, kein Ego. Nur Team. Innovation – Wir denken lieber „Warum eigentlich nicht?“ statt „Das war schon immer so.“ Wir lieben neue Ideen, unkonventionelle Wege – und bleiben nie stehen. (WH)yfood? Was wir dir bieten Wir fördern Chancengleichheit und schätzen Vielfalt. Wir verpflichten uns, ein integratives Umfeld für alle Mitarbeitende zu schaffen. yfood wächst international: Obwohl Deutschland unsers „Home Base“ ist, haben wir mit unseren internationalen Märkten ein dynamisches und buntes Umfeld geschaffen, in dem viele spannende Themen auf Dich warten. Urlaub ist wichtig. Daher erhältst du bei uns 30 Tage bezahlten Urlaub im Jahr. yfood hält dich fit . Mit einer subventionierten Mitgliedschaft bei EGYM-Wellpass kannst du dir für nur 29€ im Monat Gutes tun. Dazu bieten wir im Rahmen unseres Gesundheitsmanagements & Healthy@yfood Workshops und Aktionen (z.B. Yoga, Breathwork, Soccer, Pickleball) an. Weg vom Fleck . Wir stellen dir einen Firmenwagen auch zur privaten Nutzung zur Verfügung und bieten dir über JobRad die Möglichkeit, vergünstigt ein Fahrrad zu leasen. Trainiere deine Geschmacksnerven . Es gibt so viel yfood wie du tragen kannst, natürlich auch für dich gratis. Probiere also neue Produkte, Sorten oder Geschmäcker. Come as you are. Ob im Anzug oder Einhorn-Onesie. Einen Dresscode kennen wir nicht. KONTAKT Katharina Bauer Senior Talent Acquisition Managerj yfood steht für die Chancengleichheit aller ein. Wir begrüßen und feiern Vielfalt und setzen uns dafür ein, ein inklusives Arbeitsumfeld für alle Mitarbeiter:innen zu schaffen.
